name: microduck_rl
one_liner: The training code used to teach a small, toy-sized two-legged robot how to walk, stand up, and do tricks, using reinforcement learning in simulation.
buyer: A STEM education company or robotics research lab that wants a compelling, working walking-robot demo without building the sim2real pipeline from scratch.
business_use_cases: A STEM education company uses the trained walking robot as a flagship demo for teaching AI and robotics in schools.
A robotics research lab reuses the sim2real recipe — actuator physics, domain randomization — to bootstrap training for their own robot.
A robotics content creator builds and showcases the robot for a maker audience, drawing sponsorship revenue.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a robot kit bundled with an education curriculum built around the trained walking demo.
Offer sim2real reinforcement-learning consulting to other small-robot teams.

steal_this: This needs a CUDA GPU, real robot hardware, and deep RL know-how — not a weekend project unless you're already in robotics; the realistic play is packaging the trained policy plus hardware as an education kit.
